title: Judges 6 — The call of Gid'on (Gideon): the fire from the rock and the fleece

translation.sourceText: Hebrew Masoretic text (Westminster Leningrad Codex base, Public Domain) — Tanach with Ta'amei Hamikra

verdicts.reasoning: wayyaʿăśû ... hāraʿ bəʿênê YHWH wayyittənēm YHWH bəyaḏ-miḏyān šeḇaʿ šānîm: exact.
wattāʿāz yaḏ-miḏyān ... hamminhārôṯ (hapax) ... hamməʿārôṯ ... hamməṣāḏôṯ: 'dens ... caves ... strongholds' (ASV). Exact.
wəhāyâ ʾim-zāraʿ yiśrāʾēl wəʿālâ ... wəʿālû ʿālāyw: frequentative 'whenever ... would come up'. Exact.

wəlōʾ-yašʾîrû miḥyâ 'no sustenance' (ASV) is the livelihood sense of miḥyâ (BDB 'preservation of life; sustenance'); the appended central clause is justified. ʿaḏ-bôʾăḵā ʿazzâ 'until you come to Azzah'. Exact.

citations: Tov, Textual Criticism of the Hebrew Bible (3rd ed., 2012), on Ketiv/Qere
verdicts.reasoning: The line is correct: the Qere ûḇāʾû (perfect consecutive, frequentative 'they would come') is translated. But the note transcribes the Ketiv יבאו as *yʾbw*; the consonants are y-b-ʾ-w, so read *ybʾw* (imperfect yāḇōʾû). Same correction needed in the shared `ketiv-qere-qere-translated-former-prophets` entry (all three overlays). Note-only fix; English line approved.
wayyiddal yiśrāʾēl məʾōḏ ... wayyizʿăqû: exact.
ʿal ʾōḏôṯ miḏyān 'on account of Midyan'. The note's statement that vv 7-10 are absent from 4QJudgᵃ is accurate; MT translated. Correct.
ʾîš nāḇîʾ 'a man, a prophet'; ʾānōḵî heʿĕlêṯî ... mibbêṯ ʿăḇāḏîm 'house of slaves'. Exact.
wāʾaṣṣil ... wāʾăḡārēš ... wāʾettənâ: exact.
lōʾ ṯîrʾû ʾeṯ-ʾĕlōhê hāʾĕmōrî: lower-case 'elohim' for a non-YHWH referent under the ratified Kings clause 4; the closing wəlōʾ šəmaʿtem bəqôlî is correctly placed outside the inner quotation. Exact.
wayyāḇōʾ malʾaḵ YHWH wayyēšeḇ taḥaṯ hāʾēlâ ... ḥōḇēṭ ḥiṭṭîm baggaṯ ləhānîs: 'the oak' (as 1 Kgs 13:14); 'beating out wheat in the winepress'. Exact.
wayyērāʾ ʾēlāyw malʾaḵ YHWH ... YHWH ʿimməḵā gibbôr heḥāyil: exact.
bî ʾăḏōnî: MT vocalizes the human address (source re-checked), against v 15 ʾăḏōnāy; the line follows the vocalization. wəʾayyê ḵol-nip̄ləʾōṯāyw; nəṭāšānû 'has cast us off'. Exact.

wayyip̄en ʾēlāyw YHWH: MT names YHWH where the LXX has 'the angel of the Lord'; the alternation is characteristic of the malʾaḵ YHWH narratives and is not harmonized. lēḵ bəḵōḥăḵā zeh 'Go in this your might'. Correct.
bî ʾăḏōnāy (divine vocalization) 'Oh, Lord'; ʾalpî haddal bimnaššeh 'my clan is the poorest'. Exact.
kî ʾehyeh ʿimmāḵ wəhikkîṯā ʾeṯ-miḏyān kəʾîš ʾeḥāḏ: exact.
wəʿāśîṯā llî ʾôṯ šāʾattâ məḏabbēr ʿimmî: 'that it is you who speak with me' (šā- relative). Exact.
minḥāṯî 'my present' (ASV) keeps the hospitality sense; the note states the cultic sense the scene moves into. ʾal-nāʾ ṯāmuš mizzeh. Exact.
gəḏî-ʿizzîm wəʾêp̄aṯ-qemaḥ maṣṣôṯ ... bassal ... bappārûr ... wayyaggaš: exact.
malʾaḵ hāʾĕlōhîm (articular) 'the messenger of the Elohim' (clause 1); hasselaʿ hallāz 'this rock'; wəʾeṯ-hammāraq šəp̄ôḵ. Exact.

Re-parsed: wayyišlaḥ malʾaḵ YHWH ʾeṯ-qəṣēh hammišʿeneṯ ʾăšer bəyāḏô wayyiggaʿ ... wattaʿal hāʾēš min-haṣṣûr wattōʾḵal ... hālaḵ mēʿênāyw. 'staff', 'fire went up out of the rock', 'departed from his sight' are the ASV-literal renderings. The reception note accurately summarizes TBWTT ch. 3 (feeding tube, flames) and the line carries none of it.
wayyarʾ ... kî-malʾaḵ YHWH hûʾ (with the in-verse section mark) ... ʾăhāh ʾăḏōnāy YHWH kî-ʿal-kēn rāʾîṯî ... pānîm ʾel-pānîm: 'Forasmuch as' (ASV) renders the elliptical kî-ʿal-kēn. Exact.
šālôm ləḵā ʾal-tîrāʾ lōʾ tāmûṯ: exact.
wayyiqrāʾ-lô YHWH šālôm 'and called it YHWH-Shalom': name transliterated, meaning in the note. ʿôḏennû bəʿop̄raṯ ʾăḇî hāʿezrî. Exact.
par-haššôr ... ûp̄ar haššēnî šeḇaʿ šānîm: the ASV appositional reading (one bull) is defensible from vv 26, 28, and the two-bull/emendation views are recorded. ʾăšer-ʿālāyw 'beside it'. Exact.
ʿal rōʾš hammāʿôz hazzeh bammaʿărāḵâ 'in the orderly manner' (ASV); wəhaʿălîṯā ʿôlâ baʿăṣê hāʾăšērâ. Exact.
wayhî kaʾăšer yārēʾ ... mēʿăśôṯ yômām wayyaʿaś lāylâ: exact.
nuttaṣ ... kōrāṯâ ... hōʿălâ: passives rendered as passives. Exact.
wayyiḏrəšû wayḇaqšû 'inquired and searched'. Exact.
hôṣēʾ ʾeṯ-binḵā wəyāmōṯ: exact.

hăʾattem tərîḇûn labbaʿal ... ʾim-ʾĕlōhîm hûʾ yāreḇ lô kî nāṯaṣ ʾeṯ-mizbəḥô. 'If he is an elohim' (clause 4) is correct. 'because someone has broken down his altar' reads the 3ms verb as an indefinite subject, as the ASV/KJV 'one' do; defensible. Non-blocking: v 32 renders the identical clause 'because he has broken down', so add one sentence to the note stating that v 31 takes the subject as indefinite (Yo'ash avoiding naming his son).
wayyiqrāʾ-lô ... yərubbaʿal lēʾmōr yāreḇ bô habbaʿal: the aetiology is rendered literally; Yerubbeshet (2 Sam 11:21) correctly cited.
neʾespû yaḥdāw wayyaʿaḇrû wayyaḥănû bəʿēmeq yizrəʿeʾl: exact.

Re-parsed: wərûaḥ YHWH lāḇəšâ ʾeṯ-giḏʿôn. 'clothed' is the literal Qal of lāḇēš (KJV margin; Block), and the same idiom occurs at 1 Chr 12:19 and 2 Chr 24:20; the ASV 'came upon' levels four distinct verbs. 'the ruach of YHWH' follows the ratified Kings transliteration. Not lens leakage: no reading is added, and the ambiguity of rûaḥ is left open.
ûmalʾāḵîm šālaḥ ... wayyaʿălû liqrāʾṯām: human envoys 'messengers'. Exact.
wayyōʾmer giḏʿôn ʾel-hāʾĕlōhîm (articular): 'to the Elohim' (clause 1); ʾim-yešḵā môšîaʿ bəyāḏî. Exact.

hinnê ʾānōḵî maṣṣîḡ ʾeṯ-gizzaṯ haṣṣemer baggōren ... wəʿal-kol-hāʾāreṣ ḥōreḇ: 'on all the ground' is right. Non-blocking: the `eretz` citation was correctly removed from glossaryRefs ('ground', not 'land'), but the note still ends with '(`eretz`)'; delete it.
wayyāzar ... wayyimeṣ ṭal min-haggizzâ məlôʾ hassēp̄el māyim: 'pressed ... wrung ... a bowlful of water'. Exact.
ʾal-yiḥar ʾappəḵā bî waʾăḏabbərâ ʾaḵ happāʿam ʾănasseh nnāʾ-raq-happaʿam baggizzâ: exact; articular hāʾĕlōhîm 'the Elohim'.

paragraphs.text: וַיַּעֲשׂ֧וּ בְנֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל הָרַ֖ע בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וַיִּתְּנֵ֧ם יְהוָ֛ה בְּיַד־מִדְיָ֖ן שֶׁ֥בַע שָׁנִֽים׃

i18n.en: And the children of Yisra'el did what was evil in the sight of YHWH; and YHWH gave them into the hand of Midyan seven years.

notes.official: *wayyaʿăśû bənê-yiśrāʾēl hāraʿ bəʿênê YHWH* 'And the children of Yisra'el did what was evil in the sight of YHWH': the framework formula of Judges (2:11; 3:7, 12; 4:1). *wayyittənēm YHWH bəyaḏ-miḏyān* 'and YHWH gave them into the hand of Midyan' (`be-yedkhem-nittanu`). Midyan = Midian; Yisra'el = Israel.

paragraphs.text: וַתָּ֥עָז יַד־מִדְיָ֖ן עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל מִפְּנֵ֨י מִדְיָ֜ן עָשֽׂוּ לָהֶ֣ם ׀ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל אֶת־הַמִּנְהָרוֹת֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בֶּֽהָרִ֔ים וְאֶת־הַמְּעָר֖וֹת וְאֶת־הַמְּצָדֽוֹת׃

i18n.en: And the hand of Midyan prevailed against Yisra'el; because of Midyan the children of Yisra'el made for themselves the dens which are in the mountains, and the caves, and the strongholds.

notes.official: *hamminhārôṯ* 'the dens' (ASV): the word occurs only here, perhaps 'clefts' or 'shelters' cut in the hillsides.

paragraphs.text: וְהָיָ֖ה אִם־זָרַ֣ע יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְעָלָ֨ה מִדְיָ֧ן וַֽעֲמָלֵ֛ק וּבְנֵי־קֶ֖דֶם וְעָל֥וּ עָלָֽיו׃

i18n.en: And so it was, whenever Yisra'el had sown, that Midyan and Amaleq and the children of the east would come up; they would come up against them.

notes.official: Amaleq = Amalek. *bənê-qeḏem* 'the children of the east' (ASV), the nomadic peoples east of the Yarden, translated (`hebrew-proper-name-transliteration-convention-former-prophets`).

paragraphs.text: וַיַּחֲנ֣וּ עֲלֵיהֶ֗ם וַיַּשְׁחִ֙יתוּ֙ אֶת־יְב֣וּל הָאָ֔רֶץ עַד־בּוֹאֲךָ֖ עַזָּ֑ה וְלֹֽא־יַשְׁאִ֤ירוּ מִֽחְיָה֙ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְשֶׂ֥ה וָשׁ֖וֹר וַחֲמֽוֹר׃

i18n.en: And they would encamp against them and destroy the produce of the land, until you come to Azzah, and would leave no sustenance in Yisra'el, neither sheep nor ox nor donkey.

notes.official: *ʿaḏ-bôʾăḵā ʿazzâ* 'until you come to Azzah' (Azzah = Gaza). *wəlōʾ-yašʾîrû miḥyâ bəyiśrāʾēl* 'and would leave no sustenance in Yisra'el' (ASV): *miḥyâ*, one of five occurrences of the noun, here in its livelihood sense. The central `michyah-preservation-of-life-rare-noun` already names Judg 6:4 in its distribution; the wave diff proposes a clause for this sense.

paragraphs.text: כִּ֡י הֵם֩ וּמִקְנֵיהֶ֨ם יַעֲל֜וּ וְאָהֳלֵיהֶ֗ם יבאו [וּבָ֤אוּ] כְדֵֽי־אַרְבֶּה֙ לָרֹ֔ב וְלָהֶ֥ם וְלִגְמַלֵּיהֶ֖ם אֵ֣ין מִסְפָּ֑ר וַיָּבֹ֥אוּ בָאָ֖רֶץ לְשַׁחֲתָֽהּ׃

i18n.en: For they would come up with their livestock and their tents, and they would come like locusts for multitude; both they and their camels were without number; and they came into the land to destroy it.

notes.official: *ûḇāʾû* 'and they came' translates the Qere; the Ketiv *ybʾw* (*yāḇōʾû*) 'they would come' is an imperfect with the same sense (`ketiv-qere-qere-translated-former-prophets`). *kəḏê-ʾarbeh lārōḇ* 'like locusts for multitude'; *wəliḡmallêhem ʾên mispār* 'and their camels were without number'.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּדַּ֧ל יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל מְאֹ֖ד מִפְּנֵ֣י מִדְיָ֑ן וַיִּזְעֲק֥וּ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל אֶל־יְהוָֽה׃ (פ)

i18n.en: And Yisra'el was brought very low because of Midyan; and the children of Yisra'el cried out to YHWH.

paragraphs.text: וַיְהִ֕י כִּֽי־זָעֲק֥וּ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל אֶל־יְהוָ֑ה עַ֖ל אֹד֥וֹת מִדְיָֽן׃

i18n.en: And it came to pass, when the children of Yisra'el cried out to YHWH on account of Midyan,

notes.official: Verses 7-10 are absent from 4QJudgᵃ, which passes from v 6 to v 11, and many commentators regard the prophet's speech as a later addition. The MT is translated (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-former-prophets`).

paragraphs.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֧ח יְהוָ֛ה אִ֥ישׁ נָבִ֖יא אֶל־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיֹּ֨אמֶר לָהֶ֜ם כֹּה־אָמַ֥ר יְהוָ֣ה ׀ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל אָנֹכִ֞י הֶעֱלֵ֤יתִי אֶתְכֶם֙ מִמִּצְרַ֔יִם וָאֹצִ֥יא אֶתְכֶ֖ם מִבֵּ֥ית עֲבָדִֽים׃

i18n.en: that YHWH sent a man, a prophet, to the children of Yisra'el; and he said to them, "Thus says YHWH, the Elohim of Yisra'el: 'I brought you up from Mitzrayim, and brought you out of the house of slaves;

notes.official: *ʾîš nāḇîʾ* 'a man, a prophet' (`navi-first-occurrence-abraham`), anonymous. *kōh-ʾāmar YHWH ʾĕlōhê yiśrāʾēl* 'Thus says YHWH, the Elohim of Yisra'el' (`elohei-yisrael`; clause 3 of `elohim-referent-and-article-conventions-former-prophets`). *mibbêṯ ʿăḇāḏîm* 'out of the house of slaves' (Ex 20:2). Mitzrayim = Egypt. On vv 7-10 see v 7 (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-former-prophets`).

paragraphs.text: וָאַצִּ֤ל אֶתְכֶם֙ מִיַּ֣ד מִצְרַ֔יִם וּמִיַּ֖ד כָּל־לֹחֲצֵיכֶ֑ם וָאֲגָרֵ֤שׁ אוֹתָם֙ מִפְּנֵיכֶ֔ם וָאֶתְּנָ֥ה לָכֶ֖ם אֶת־אַרְצָֽם׃

i18n.en: and I delivered you out of the hand of Mitzrayim and out of the hand of all who oppressed you, and drove them out from before you, and gave you their land;

paragraphs.text: וָאֹמְרָ֣ה לָכֶ֗ם אֲנִי֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶ֔ם לֹ֤א תִֽירְאוּ֙ אֶת־אֱלֹהֵ֣י הָאֱמֹרִ֔י אֲשֶׁ֥ר אַתֶּ֖ם יוֹשְׁבִ֣ים בְּאַרְצָ֑ם וְלֹ֥א שְׁמַעְתֶּ֖ם בְּקוֹלִֽי׃ (פ)

i18n.en: and I said to you, "I am YHWH your Elohim; you shall not fear the elohim of the Emorites, in whose land you dwell." But you have not listened to my voice.'"

notes.official: *ʾănî YHWH ʾĕlōhêḵem* 'I am YHWH your Elohim' (clause 3). *lōʾ ṯîrʾû ʾeṯ-ʾĕlōhê hāʾĕmōrî* 'you shall not fear the elohim of the Emorites': lower-case 'elohim' for gods other than YHWH (clause 4 of `elohim-referent-and-article-conventions-former-prophets`; central `elohim-aherim-other-gods-monolatry-vs-monotheism-scholarly-dispute-cross-corpus`). 'the Emorites' (`hebrew-proper-name-transliteration-convention-former-prophets`).

paragraphs.text: וַיָּבֹ֞א מַלְאַ֣ךְ יְהוָ֗ה וַיֵּ֙שֶׁב֙ תַּ֤חַת הָֽאֵלָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּעָפְרָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר לְיוֹאָ֖שׁ אֲבִ֣י הָֽעֶזְרִ֑י וְגִדְע֣וֹן בְּנ֗וֹ חֹבֵ֤ט חִטִּים֙ בַּגַּ֔ת לְהָנִ֖יס מִפְּנֵ֥י מִדְיָֽן׃

i18n.en: And the messenger of YHWH came and sat under the oak which was in Ofrah, which belonged to Yo'ash the Avi'ezrite; and his son Gid'on was beating out wheat in the winepress, to hide it from Midyan.

notes.official: *malʾaḵ YHWH* 'the messenger of YHWH' (`malakh-yhwh-messenger`; ASV 'the angel of Jehovah'). *taḥaṯ hāʾēlâ* 'under the oak' (ASV), as Kings renders the same noun at 1 Kgs 13:14; the *ʾēlâ* is often identified as the terebinth. Ofrah = Ophrah; Yo'ash = Joash; *ʾăḇî hāʿezrî* 'the Avi'ezrite' (Abiezrite); Gid'on = Gideon (`hebrew-proper-name-transliteration-convention-former-prophets`). *ḥōḇēṭ ḥiṭṭîm baggaṯ* 'beating out wheat in the winepress': threshing in a hidden winepress rather than on an open threshing floor, out of sight of Midyan.

paragraphs.text: וַיֵּרָ֥א אֵלָ֖יו מַלְּאַ֣ךְ יְהוָ֑ה וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֔יו יְהוָ֥ה עִמְּךָ֖ גִּבּ֥וֹר הֶחָֽיִל׃

i18n.en: And the messenger of YHWH appeared to him and said to him, "YHWH is with you, you mighty man of valor."

notes.official: *wayyērāʾ ʾēlāyw malʾaḵ YHWH* 'And the messenger of YHWH appeared to him'. *YHWH ʿimməḵā gibbôr heḥāyil* 'YHWH is with you, you mighty man of valor' (`elohim-imkha-divine-presence-formula`).

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֵלָ֤יו גִּדְעוֹן֙ בִּ֣י אֲדֹנִ֔י וְיֵ֤שׁ יְהוָה֙ עִמָּ֔נוּ וְלָ֥מָּה מְצָאַ֖תְנוּ כָּל־זֹ֑את וְאַיֵּ֣ה כָֽל־נִפְלְאֹתָ֡יו אֲשֶׁר֩ סִפְּרוּ־לָ֨נוּ אֲבוֹתֵ֜ינוּ לֵאמֹ֗ר הֲלֹ֤א מִמִּצְרַ֙יִם֙ הֶעֱלָ֣נוּ יְהוָ֔ה וְעַתָּה֙ נְטָשָׁ֣נוּ יְהוָ֔ה וַֽיִּתְּנֵ֖נוּ בְּכַף־מִדְיָֽן׃

i18n.en: And Gid'on said to him, "Oh, my lord, if YHWH is with us, why then has all this befallen us? And where are all his wonders which our fathers told us of, saying, 'Did not YHWH bring us up from Mitzrayim?' But now YHWH has cast us off and given us into the hand of Midyan."

notes.official: *bî ʾăḏōnî* 'Oh, my lord': the MT vocalizes *ʾăḏōnî*, the address to a human superior, and at v 15 *ʾăḏōnāy*, the divine form ('Oh, Lord'), after the narrator has said that YHWH turned to him (v 14). The vocalizations follow the scene's movement toward recognition and are kept (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-former-prophets`). *wəyēš YHWH ʿimmānû* 'if YHWH is with us' answers v 12 (`elohim-imkha-divine-presence-formula`). *wəʾayyê ḵol-nip̄ləʾōṯāyw* 'And where are all his wonders': the root *plʾ* returns in the messenger's name at 13:18 (`peli-wonderful-name-judges-13-18`).

paragraphs.text: וַיִּ֤פֶן אֵלָיו֙ יְהוָ֔ה וַיֹּ֗אמֶר לֵ֚ךְ בְּכֹחֲךָ֣ זֶ֔ה וְהוֹשַׁעְתָּ֥ אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מִכַּ֣ף מִדְיָ֑ן הֲלֹ֖א שְׁלַחְתִּֽיךָ׃

i18n.en: And YHWH turned to him and said, "Go in this your might, and save Yisra'el from the hand of Midyan; have I not sent you?"

notes.official: *wayyip̄en ʾēlāyw YHWH* 'And YHWH turned to him': the MT names YHWH where the LXX reads 'the messenger of YHWH'. The passage from messenger to YHWH within one scene is characteristic of the *malʾaḵ YHWH* narratives (central `malakh-yhwh-messenger`, which discusses this passage) and is kept (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-former-prophets`). *hălōʾ šəlaḥtîḵā* 'have I not sent you?' is the commissioning formula (cf. Ex 3:10-12).

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלָיו֙ בִּ֣י אֲדֹנָ֔י בַּמָּ֥ה אוֹשִׁ֖יעַ אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל הִנֵּ֤ה אַלְפִּי֙ הַדַּ֣ל בִּמְנַשֶּׁ֔ה וְאָנֹכִ֥י הַצָּעִ֖יר בְּבֵ֥ית אָבִֽי׃

i18n.en: And he said to him, "Oh, Lord, with what shall I save Yisra'el? Behold, my clan is the poorest in Menasheh, and I am the least in my father's house."

notes.official: *bî ʾăḏōnāy* 'Oh, Lord' (divine vocalization; see v 13). *hinnê ʾalpî haddal bimnaššeh* 'Behold, my clan is the poorest in Menasheh' (Menasheh = Manasseh): *ʾelep̄* 'thousand' as a clan unit.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלָיו֙ יְהוָ֔ה כִּ֥י אֶהְיֶ֖ה עִמָּ֑ךְ וְהִכִּיתָ֥ אֶת־מִדְיָ֖ן כְּאִ֥ישׁ אֶחָֽד׃

i18n.en: And YHWH said to him, "Surely I will be with you, and you shall strike Midyan as one man."

notes.official: *kî ʾehyeh ʿimmāḵ* 'Surely I will be with you': the *ʾehyeh* of Ex 3:12, 14 (`elohim-imkha-divine-presence-formula`). *kəʾîš ʾeḥāḏ* 'as one man', that is, all at once.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֔יו אִם־נָ֛א מָצָ֥אתִי חֵ֖ן בְּעֵינֶ֑יךָ וְעָשִׂ֤יתָ לִּי֙ א֔וֹת שָׁאַתָּ֖ה מְדַבֵּ֥ר עִמִּֽי׃

i18n.en: And he said to him, "If now I have found favor in your sight, then make me a sign that it is you who speak with me.

notes.official: *ʾim-nāʾ māṣāʾṯî ḥēn bəʿênêḵā* 'If now I have found favor in your sight' (`matza-chen-be-einei-x-favor-formula`). *wəʿāśîṯā llî ʾôṯ* 'then make me a sign': the request is answered by the fire of v 21.

paragraphs.text: אַל־נָ֨א תָמֻ֤שׁ מִזֶּה֙ עַד־בֹּאִ֣י אֵלֶ֔יךָ וְהֹֽצֵאתִי֙ אֶת־מִנְחָתִ֔י וְהִנַּחְתִּ֖י לְפָנֶ֑יךָ וַיֹּאמַ֕ר אָנֹכִ֥י אֵשֵׁ֖ב עַ֥ד שׁוּבֶֽךָ׃

i18n.en: Do not depart from here, I pray you, until I come to you and bring out my present and set it before you." And he said, "I will stay until you return."

notes.official: *minḥāṯî* 'my present' (ASV), per central `minchah-tribute-gift-of-appeasement` (a gift to an honoured guest). The noun is also the term for an offering (central `minchah-shaah`; NRSV, NJPS 'offering'), and the narrative moves from hospitality to sacrifice in vv 19-21, so both senses are present.

paragraphs.text: וְגִדְע֣וֹן בָּ֗א וַיַּ֤עַשׂ גְּדִֽי־עִזִּים֙ וְאֵיפַת־קֶ֣מַח מַצּ֔וֹת הַבָּשָׂר֙ שָׂ֣ם בַּסַּ֔ל וְהַמָּרַ֖ק שָׂ֣ם בַּפָּר֑וּר וַיּוֹצֵ֥א אֵלָ֛יו אֶל־תַּ֥חַת הָאֵלָ֖ה וַיַּגַּֽשׁ׃ (ס)

i18n.en: And Gid'on went in and prepared a kid of the goats, and unleavened cakes of an ephah of flour; the meat he put in a basket, and the broth he put in a pot, and he brought it out to him under the oak, and presented it.

notes.official: *gəḏî-ʿizzîm* 'a kid of the goats'; *ʾêp̄aṯ-qemaḥ maṣṣôṯ* 'unleavened cakes of an ephah of flour', a lavish quantity; *bassal* 'in a basket', *bappārûr* 'in a pot'. *wayyaggaš* 'and presented it' is also a cultic verb (Amos 5:25).

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֵלָ֜יו מַלְאַ֣ךְ הָאֱלֹהִ֗ים קַ֣ח אֶת־הַבָּשָׂ֤ר וְאֶת־הַמַּצּוֹת֙ וְהַנַּח֙ אֶל־הַסֶּ֣לַע הַלָּ֔ז וְאֶת־הַמָּרַ֖ק שְׁפ֑וֹךְ וַיַּ֖עַשׂ כֵּֽן׃

i18n.en: And the messenger of the Elohim said to him, "Take the meat and the unleavened cakes, and lay them on this rock, and pour out the broth." And he did so.

notes.official: *malʾaḵ hāʾĕlōhîm* 'the messenger of the Elohim': the Hebrew has the article, which is kept (clause 1 of `elohim-referent-and-article-conventions-former-prophets`); the noun is governed by `malakh-elohim-messenger`. *hasselaʿ hallāz* 'this rock': *selaʿ*, where v 21 has *ṣûr*; both are 'rock' (`mishenet-staff-fire-from-the-rock-judges-6-21`). *wəʾeṯ-hammāraq šəp̄ôḵ* 'and pour out the broth', as a libation.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֞ח מַלְאַ֣ךְ יְהוָ֗ה אֶת־קְצֵ֤ה הַמִּשְׁעֶ֙נֶת֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּיָד֔וֹ וַיִּגַּ֥ע בַּבָּשָׂ֖ר וּבַמַּצּ֑וֹת וַתַּ֨עַל הָאֵ֜שׁ מִן־הַצּ֗וּר וַתֹּ֤אכַל אֶת־הַבָּשָׂר֙ וְאֶת־הַמַּצּ֔וֹת וּמַלְאַ֣ךְ יְהוָ֔ה הָלַ֖ךְ מֵעֵינָֽיו׃

i18n.en: Then the messenger of YHWH put out the end of the staff that was in his hand and touched the meat and the unleavened cakes; and fire went up out of the rock and consumed the meat and the unleavened cakes; and the messenger of YHWH departed from his sight.

notes.official:
*wayyišlaḥ malʾaḵ YHWH ʾeṯ-qəṣēh hammišʿeneṯ ʾăšer bəyāḏô* 'Then the messenger of YHWH put out the end of the staff that was in his hand': *mišʿeneṯ* is a staff or walking stick, something to lean on (*šʿn* 'lean'; Ex 21:19; 2 Kgs 4:29) (`mishenet-staff-fire-from-the-rock-judges-6-21`). *wattaʿal hāʾēš min-haṣṣûr* 'and fire went up out of the rock' consumed the meat and the cakes: the fire marks acceptance of the meal as an offering, as at Lev 9:24 and 1 Kgs 18:38, and gives the sign asked for in v 17 (Block, *Judges, Ruth*, NAC 6, 1999). *ûmalʾaḵ YHWH hālaḵ mēʿênāyw* 'and the messenger of YHWH departed from his sight' (ASV): literally 'went from his eyes'; the French canon has 'disparut'.

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** The Book Which Tells the Truth (ch. 3) quotes this verse and reads the scene as Gid'on handing food to one of the creators, who used a scientific means to extract nourishment from the offering through a flexible tube, the 'staff', a process that gave off flames which people took for sacrifice. The line renders *mišʿeneṯ*, *ʾēš* and *ṣûr* literally and does not encode that reading.

paragraphs.text: וַיַּ֣רְא גִּדְע֔וֹן כִּֽי־מַלְאַ֥ךְ יְהוָ֖ה ה֑וּא (ס) וַיֹּ֣אמֶר גִּדְע֗וֹן אֲהָהּ֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה כִּֽי־עַל־כֵּ֤ן רָאִ֙יתִי֙ מַלְאַ֣ךְ יְהוָ֔ה פָּנִ֖ים אֶל־פָּנִֽים׃

i18n.en: And Gid'on saw that he was the messenger of YHWH; and Gid'on said, "Alas, Lord YHWH! Forasmuch as I have seen the messenger of YHWH face to face."

notes.official: *wayyarʾ giḏʿôn kî-malʾaḵ YHWH hûʾ* 'And Gid'on saw that he was the messenger of YHWH'; at this point the MT has a section mark within the verse (`piska-b-emtza-pasuq-masoretic-paragraph-break`). *ʾăhāh ʾăḏōnāy YHWH* 'Alas, Lord YHWH!' (`adonai-yhwh-divine-name`). *kî-ʿal-kēn rāʾîṯî* 'Forasmuch as I have seen' (ASV): an elliptical clause ('for this is why ... I have seen'), whose implied fear is answered in v 23 (NJPS 'For I have seen'). *pānîm ʾel-pānîm* 'face to face' (`peniel-panim-el-panim-divine-face-encounter`; Gen 32:31; Ex 33:11).

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר ל֧וֹ יְהוָ֛ה שָׁל֥וֹם לְךָ֖ אַל־תִּירָ֑א לֹ֖א תָּמֽוּת׃

i18n.en: And YHWH said to him, "Peace be to you; do not fear; you shall not die."

notes.official: *šālôm ləḵā ʾal-tîrāʾ lōʾ tāmûṯ* 'Peace be to you; do not fear; you shall not die' (`al-tira-fear-not-divine-encouragement-formula`): the reassurance gives the altar its name in v 24.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּבֶן֩ שָׁ֨ם גִּדְע֤וֹן מִזְבֵּ֙חַ֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה וַיִּקְרָא־ל֥וֹ יְהוָ֖ה שָׁל֑וֹם עַ֚ד הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֔ה עוֹדֶ֕נּוּ בְּעָפְרָ֖ת אֲבִ֥י הָעֶזְרִֽי׃ (פ)

i18n.en: Then Gid'on built an altar there to YHWH and called it YHWH-Shalom. Unto this day it is still in Ofrah of the Avi'ezrites.

notes.official: *wayyiqrāʾ-lô YHWH šālôm* 'and called it YHWH-Shalom' (ASV 'Jehovah-shalom'): transliterated as the name of the altar, as genesis-woh does with 'YHWH-yir'eh' (Gen 22:14); the meaning, 'YHWH is peace', takes up v 23 (`hebrew-proper-name-transliteration-convention-former-prophets`). *ʿaḏ hayyôm hazzeh* 'Unto this day' (`ad-ha-yom-ha-zeh-aetiological-formula`). *bəʿop̄raṯ ʾăḇî hāʿezrî* 'in Ofrah of the Avi'ezrites'.

paragraphs.text: וַיְהִי֮ בַּלַּ֣יְלָה הַהוּא֒ וַיֹּ֧אמֶר ל֣וֹ יְהוָ֗ה קַ֤ח אֶת־פַּר־הַשּׁוֹר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לְאָבִ֔יךָ וּפַ֥ר הַשֵּׁנִ֖י שֶׁ֣בַע שָׁנִ֑ים וְהָרַסְתָּ֗ אֶת־מִזְבַּ֤ח הַבַּ֙עַל֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לְאָבִ֔יךָ וְאֶת־הָאֲשֵׁרָ֥ה אֲשֶׁר־עָלָ֖יו תִּכְרֹֽת׃

i18n.en: And it came to pass that same night that YHWH said to him, "Take your father's bull, even the second bull, seven years old, and throw down the altar of Ba'al that your father has, and cut down the Asherah that is beside it;

notes.official: *qaḥ ʾeṯ-par-haššôr ʾăšer ləʾāḇîḵā ûp̄ar haššēnî šeḇaʿ šānîm* 'Take your father's bull, even the second bull, seven years old': the ASV's appositional reading (one bull) is kept, since vv 26 and 28 mention only 'the second bull'. Others read two animals (NJPS 'your father's young bull and another bull seven years old') or emend (Boling, *Judges*, AB 6A, 1975; Block, *Judges, Ruth*). *mizbaḥ habbaʿal* 'the altar of Ba'al' (`habbaal-baal-hebrew-bible-rendering-former-prophets`). *wəʾeṯ-hāʾăšērâ ʾăšer-ʿālāyw tiḵrōṯ* 'and cut down the Asherah that is beside it': here a wooden cult object beside the altar, cut down and used as firewood (v 26), capitalized 'the Asherah' as in the ASV and in Kings (`hebrew-proper-name-transliteration-convention-former-prophets`).

paragraphs.text: וּבָנִ֨יתָ מִזְבֵּ֜חַ לַיהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֗יךָ עַ֣ל רֹ֧אשׁ הַמָּע֛וֹז הַזֶּ֖ה בַּמַּֽעֲרָכָ֑ה וְלָֽקַחְתָּ֙ אֶת־הַפָּ֣ר הַשֵּׁנִ֔י וְהַעֲלִ֣יתָ עוֹלָ֔ה בַּעֲצֵ֥י הָאֲשֵׁרָ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר תִּכְרֹֽת׃

i18n.en: and build an altar to YHWH your Elohim on the top of this stronghold, in the orderly manner, and take the second bull, and offer a burnt-offering with the wood of the Asherah which you shall cut down."

notes.official: *ʿal rōʾš hammāʿôz hazzeh* 'on the top of this stronghold'. *bammaʿărāḵâ* 'in the orderly manner' (ASV): *maʿărāḵâ* is an arrangement or row, here probably the proper ordering of the altar stones or the wood. *YHWH ʾĕlōhêḵā* 'YHWH your Elohim' (clause 3 of `elohim-referent-and-article-conventions-former-prophets`). *ʿôlâ* 'a burnt-offering' (`olah-burnt-offering`), burned with the wood of the Asherah.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּקַּ֨ח גִּדְע֜וֹן עֲשָׂרָ֤ה אֲנָשִׁים֙ מֵֽעֲבָדָ֔יו וַיַּ֕עַשׂ כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר דִּבֶּ֥ר אֵלָ֖יו יְהוָ֑ה וַיְהִ֡י כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר יָרֵא֩ אֶת־בֵּ֨ית אָבִ֜יו וְאֶת־אַנְשֵׁ֥י הָעִ֛יר מֵעֲשׂ֥וֹת יוֹמָ֖ם וַיַּ֥עַשׂ לָֽיְלָה׃

i18n.en: Then Gid'on took ten men of his servants and did as YHWH had spoken to him; and it came to pass, because he feared his father's household and the men of the city too much to do it by day, that he did it by night.

paragraphs.text: וַיַּשְׁכִּ֜ימוּ אַנְשֵׁ֤י הָעִיר֙ בַּבֹּ֔קֶר וְהִנֵּ֤ה נֻתַּץ֙ מִזְבַּ֣ח הַבַּ֔עַל וְהָאֲשֵׁרָ֥ה אֲשֶׁר־עָלָ֖יו כֹּרָ֑תָה וְאֵת֙ הַפָּ֣ר הַשֵּׁנִ֔י הֹֽעֲלָ֔ה עַל־הַמִּזְבֵּ֖חַ הַבָּנֽוּי׃

i18n.en: And the men of the city rose early in the morning, and behold, the altar of Ba'al was broken down, and the Asherah that was beside it was cut down, and the second bull was offered up on the altar that had been built.

notes.official: *nuttaṣ mizbaḥ habbaʿal* 'the altar of Ba'al was broken down' (`habbaal-baal-hebrew-bible-rendering-former-prophets`); *hōʿălâ* 'was offered up'.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ אִ֣ישׁ אֶל־רֵעֵ֔הוּ מִ֥י עָשָׂ֖ה הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֑ה וַֽיִּדְרְשׁוּ֙ וַיְבַקְשׁ֔וּ וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ גִּדְעוֹן֙ בֶּן־יוֹאָ֔שׁ עָשָׂ֖ה הַדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּֽה׃

i18n.en: And they said to one another, "Who has done this thing?" And when they inquired and searched, they said, "Gid'on the son of Yo'ash has done this thing."

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֨אמְר֜וּ אַנְשֵׁ֤י הָעִיר֙ אֶל־יוֹאָ֔שׁ הוֹצֵ֥א אֶת־בִּנְךָ֖ וְיָמֹ֑ת כִּ֤י נָתַץ֙ אֶת־מִזְבַּ֣ח הַבַּ֔עַל וְכִ֥י כָרַ֖ת הָאֲשֵׁרָ֥ה אֲשֶׁר־עָלָֽיו׃

i18n.en: Then the men of the city said to Yo'ash, "Bring out your son, that he may die, because he has broken down the altar of Ba'al, and because he has cut down the Asherah that was beside it."

notes.official: *hôṣēʾ ʾeṯ-binḵā wəyāmōṯ* 'Bring out your son, that he may die'. The altar of Ba'al and the Asherah (`habbaal-baal-hebrew-bible-rendering-former-prophets`).

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יוֹאָ֡שׁ לְכֹל֩ אֲשֶׁר־עָמְד֨וּ עָלָ֜יו הַאַתֶּ֣ם ׀ תְּרִיב֣וּן לַבַּ֗עַל אִם־אַתֶּם֙ תּוֹשִׁיע֣וּן אוֹת֔וֹ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יָרִ֥יב ל֛וֹ יוּמַ֖ת עַד־הַבֹּ֑קֶר אִם־אֱלֹהִ֥ים הוּא֙ יָ֣רֶב ל֔וֹ כִּ֥י נָתַ֖ץ אֶֽת־מִזְבְּחֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: And Yo'ash said to all who stood against him, "Will you contend for Ba'al? Or will you save him? Whoever contends for him shall be put to death by morning. If he is an elohim, let him contend for himself, because someone has broken down his altar."

notes.official: *hăʾattem tərîḇûn labbaʿal* 'Will you contend for Ba'al?' (`habbaal-baal-hebrew-bible-rendering-former-prophets`). *ʾim-ʾĕlōhîm hûʾ yāreḇ lô* 'If he is an elohim, let him contend for himself': lower case for the non-YHWH referent (clause 4 of `elohim-referent-and-article-conventions-former-prophets`; cf. 1 Kgs 18:27 'for he is an elohim'). *ʿaḏ-habbōqer* 'by morning'. *kî nāṯaṣ ʾeṯ-mizbəḥô* 'because someone has broken down his altar': the 3ms subject is taken as indefinite here (GKC §144d), while v 32 renders the identical clause 'he', where the subject is Gid'on.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּקְרָא־ל֥וֹ בַיּוֹם־הַה֖וּא יְרֻבַּ֣עַל לֵאמֹ֑ר יָ֤רֶב בּוֹ֙ הַבַּ֔עַל כִּ֥י נָתַ֖ץ אֶֽת־מִזְבְּחֽוֹ׃ (פ)

i18n.en: Therefore on that day he called him Yerubba'al, saying, "Let Ba'al contend against him, because he has broken down his altar."

notes.official: *wayyiqrāʾ-lô ḇayyôm-hahûʾ yərubbaʿal* 'Therefore on that day he called him Yerubba'al' (Jerubbaal), explained by *yāreḇ bô habbaʿal* 'Let Ba'al contend against him' (`al-ken-qara-shemah-aetiological-naming-formula-cross-corpus`). The name probably meant 'Ba'al contends' or 'Ba'al is great', and the narrative turns it against the god; 2 Sam 11:21 has the deformed form Yerubbeshet (Block, *Judges, Ruth*) (`habbaal-baal-hebrew-bible-rendering-former-prophets`).

paragraphs.text: וְכָל־מִדְיָ֧ן וַעֲמָלֵ֛ק וּבְנֵי־קֶ֖דֶם נֶאֶסְפ֣וּ יַחְדָּ֑ו וַיַּעַבְר֥וּ וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ בְּעֵ֥מֶק יִזְרְעֶֽאל׃

i18n.en: Then all Midyan and Amaleq and the children of the east gathered together; and they crossed over and encamped in the valley of Yizre'el.

notes.official: *bəʿēmeq yizrəʿeʾl* 'in the valley of Yizre'el' (Jezreel); Midyan, Amaleq and the children of the east (v 3).

paragraphs.text: וְר֣וּחַ יְהוָ֔ה לָבְשָׁ֖ה אֶת־גִּדְע֑וֹן וַיִּתְקַע֙ בַּשּׁוֹפָ֔ר וַיִזָּעֵ֥ק אֲבִיעֶ֖זֶר אַחֲרָֽיו׃

i18n.en: But the ruach of YHWH clothed Gid'on; and he blew the shofar, and Avi'ezer was called out after him.

notes.official: *wərûaḥ YHWH lāḇəšâ ʾeṯ-giḏʿôn* 'But the ruach of YHWH clothed Gid'on' (ASV 'the Spirit of Jehovah came upon Gideon'): the noun is transliterated as in Kings, and the verb *lāḇaš* 'put on, clothe' is rendered literally, the *rûaḥ* taking Gid'on as its garment (so also 1 Chr 12:19; 2 Chr 24:20; KJV margin 'clothed'; Block, *Judges, Ruth*) (`ruach-yhwh-transliteration-former-prophets`). Judges uses distinct verbs for the coming of the *rûaḥ YHWH* (*hāyâ ʿal* 3:10; 11:29; *ṣālaḥ* 14:6, 19; 15:14; *pāʿam* 13:25), and the translation keeps them distinct. *wayyiṯqaʿ baššôp̄ār* 'and he blew the shofar', the signal for mustering (proposed central `shofar-rams-horn-signal-instrument-cross-corpus`). *wayyizzāʿēq ʾăḇîʿezer ʾaḥărāyw* 'and Avi'ezer was called out after him' (Avi'ezer = Abiezer).

paragraphs.text: וּמַלְאָכִים֙ שָׁלַ֣ח בְּכָל־מְנַשֶּׁ֔ה וַיִזָּעֵ֥ק גַּם־ה֖וּא אַחֲרָ֑יו וּמַלְאָכִ֣ים שָׁלַ֗ח בְּאָשֵׁ֤ר וּבִזְבֻלוּן֙ וּבְנַפְתָּלִ֔י וַֽיַּעֲל֖וּ לִקְרָאתָֽם׃

i18n.en: And he sent messengers throughout all Menasheh, and they too were called out after him; and he sent messengers to Asher, and to Zevulun, and to Naftali; and they came up to meet them.

notes.official: *malʾāḵîm* 'messengers' (human envoys; `malakh-yhwh-messenger`). Menasheh, Asher, Zevulun (Zebulun), Naftali (Naphtali) (`hebrew-proper-name-transliteration-convention-former-prophets`).

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר גִּדְע֖וֹן אֶל־הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים אִם־יֶשְׁךָ֞ מוֹשִׁ֧יעַ בְּיָדִ֛י אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבַּֽרְתָּ׃

i18n.en: And Gid'on said to the Elohim, "If you will save Yisra'el by my hand, as you have spoken,

notes.official: *wayyōʾmer giḏʿôn ʾel-hāʾĕlōhîm* 'And Gid'on said to the Elohim': the Hebrew has the article here and at v 39 (clause 1 of `elohim-referent-and-article-conventions-former-prophets`). *ʾim-yešḵā môšîaʿ bəyāḏî* 'If you will save Yisra'el by my hand'.

paragraphs.text: הִנֵּ֣ה אָנֹכִ֗י מַצִּ֛יג אֶת־גִּזַּ֥ת הַצֶּ֖מֶר בַּגֹּ֑רֶן אִ֡ם טַל֩ יִהְיֶ֨ה עַֽל־הַגִּזָּ֜ה לְבַדָּ֗הּ וְעַל־כָּל־הָאָ֙רֶץ֙ חֹ֔רֶב וְיָדַעְתִּ֗י כִּֽי־תוֹשִׁ֧יעַ בְּיָדִ֛י אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבַּֽרְתָּ׃

i18n.en: behold, I am placing a fleece of wool on the threshing floor; if there is dew on the fleece only, and it is dry on all the ground, then I shall know that you will save Yisra'el by my hand, as you have spoken."

notes.official: *gizzaṯ haṣṣemer* 'a fleece of wool'; *baggōren* 'on the threshing floor'. *wəʿal-kol-hāʾāreṣ ḥōreḇ* 'and it is dry on all the ground'.

paragraphs.text: וַיְהִי־כֵ֕ן וַיַּשְׁכֵּם֙ מִֽמָּחֳרָ֔ת וַיָּ֖זַר אֶת־הַגִּזָּ֑ה וַיִּ֤מֶץ טַל֙ מִן־הַגִּזָּ֔ה מְל֥וֹא הַסֵּ֖פֶל מָֽיִם׃

i18n.en: And it was so; for he rose early on the next day, and pressed the fleece, and wrung dew out of the fleece, a bowlful of water.

notes.official: *wayyāzar ʾeṯ-haggizzâ* 'and pressed the fleece'; *məlôʾ hassēp̄el* 'a bowlful'.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר גִּדְעוֹן֙ אֶל־הָ֣אֱלֹהִ֔ים אַל־יִ֤חַר אַפְּךָ֙ בִּ֔י וַאֲדַבְּרָ֖ה אַ֣ךְ הַפָּ֑עַם אֲנַסֶּ֤ה נָּא־רַק־הַפַּ֙עַם֙ בַּגִּזָּ֔ה יְהִי־נָ֨א חֹ֤רֶב אֶל־הַגִּזָּה֙ לְבַדָּ֔הּ וְעַל־כָּל־הָאָ֖רֶץ יִֽהְיֶה־טָּֽל׃

i18n.en: And Gid'on said to the Elohim, "Do not let your anger burn against me, and let me speak just this once; let me test, I pray you, just this once more with the fleece: let it now be dry on the fleece only, and on all the ground let there be dew."

notes.official: *ʾal-yiḥar ʾappəḵā bî* 'Do not let your anger burn against me' (cf. Avraham's plea, Gen 18:30, 32). The Hebrew has the article on *hāʾĕlōhîm* (clause 1 of `elohim-referent-and-article-conventions-former-prophets`).

paragraphs.text: וַיַּ֧עַשׂ אֱלֹהִ֛ים כֵּ֖ן בַּלַּ֣יְלָה הַה֑וּא וַיְהִי־חֹ֤רֶב אֶל־הַגִּזָּה֙ לְבַדָּ֔הּ וְעַל־כָּל־הָאָ֖רֶץ הָ֥יָה טָֽל׃ (פ)

i18n.en: And the Elohim did so that night; for it was dry on the fleece only, and on all the ground there was dew.

notes.official: *wayyaʿaś ʾĕlōhîm kēn* 'And the Elohim did so': the Hebrew is anarthrous here, after the articular *hāʾĕlōhîm* of vv 36 and 39. Under clause 6 of `elohim-referent-and-article-conventions-former-prophets`, which applies the narrative rule of central `elohim-as-translation` unchanged, an anarthrous *ʾĕlōhîm* as narrative subject takes the English article; the Kings entry leaves that rule in force and limits the article-less form to predicates, genitives and direct speech. The two Hebrew forms are therefore not distinguished in English here, and this note records the difference.
